title: Voz pasiva: síntesis de la sociedad colonial

sections.content: A synthesis paragraph often needs several passive sentences in a row, each treating a different institution as its subject — administration, opportunity, infrastructure — to show how they fit together without repeating 'the Spanish' as the agent every time. These sentences are taken directly from the previous reading.

items.spanish: Los territorios fueron administrados mediante virreinatos y audiencias que respondían a una corona lejana.
items.english: The territories were administered through viceroyalties and high courts answering to a distant crown.

items.spanish: Las oportunidades económicas y políticas fueron distribuidas de forma muy desigual entre peninsulares, criollos, indígenas y africanos.
items.english: Economic and political opportunities were distributed very unequally among peninsulares, criollos, indigenous people and Africans.

items.spanish: Las estructuras educativas y sanitarias fueron mantenidas, en gran medida, por una Iglesia que actuaba casi como un segundo gobierno.
items.english: Educational and healthcare structures were maintained, to a large extent, by a Church that acted almost like a second government.

items.spanish: Buena parte del trazado urbano actual fue diseñado directamente por una ley real de 1573.
items.english: Much of today's urban layout was designed directly by a royal law of 1573.

sections.content: When you're summarizing a whole unit, passive voice lets each sentence open with the topic you're synthesizing (los territorios, las oportunidades, las estructuras) rather than forcing every sentence to start with 'España' or 'la Corona' — a small trick that keeps a synthesis paragraph from sounding repetitive.
